text.p: Defence Minister Igor Rodionov said on Friday that Russia's cash-strapped armed forces were on the brink of "uncontrollable developments", Interfax news agency said.

"Russia's leadership and society should know that the chronic lack of funds are taking the armed forces to the brink of undesirable, and even uncontrollable, developments," Interfax quoted Rodionov as saying.
Rodionov told army veterans that a cash shortage, appalling social conditions and poor maintenance were leading to a "severe crisis" in the armed forces.

"If the 1997 defence budget is not changed, Russia may lose the armed forces as an integral and active state structure, with all the consequences which would follow that," he said, but gave no details.
Russia's former national security supremo, Alexander Lebed, sacked by President Boris Yeltsin last week, has warned that the armed forces were on the brink of rebellion.
At the time Rodionov denied Lebed's predictions. He said the military was under control and there was no reason to expect any sort of mutiny in the armed forces.
